title: Security audit fixes: nothing about a player or a Co-host stays in the audit log; strangers cannot fill it
changes: A player's name and mobile number, and a Co-host's name and mobile number, no longer stay in the audit log for a year after you press Delete or Forget. Rows kept for 365 days now hold no names, numbers, e-mail addresses, IDs or places, whatever the field is called (a number or e-mail inside any text is removed too)
The calls that name a person (look up, mark, unbind, delete, add a Co-host, waiting list, invites) keep only the field names in the log, never the values
A Co-host's own calls are kept in the part of the log that is deleted 23 hours after the game, like a player's
A visitor with no key can no longer fill the audit log: a call to a game that does not exist, or to an address that does not exist, leaves no row, and one network can add only a few rows a minute
Gentler wording: no tick-boxes and no Accept button anywhere on the agreement screens; going ahead is the agreement and the Terms stay one link away

title: Security audit fixes: a closed game stays closed on a settings save
changes: A closed game can no longer be opened to anyone with the link by a settings save that sends closed as null or as empty text: closed is accepted only when it is left out or is true
The console's payInfo call reads at most 4096 bytes of the request and refuses a bigger one
The payInfo call tells a network to wait after 20 requests in a minute that could not be checked; the count is kept in memory and writes nothing to the database

title: Owner rules v1.1 joined to the live production code (f17d1906d8a7)
changes: This release joins two lines of work that had drifted apart: the code that is live on the website (commit f17d1906d8a7, deployed 5 Nov 2026) and the owner rules v1.1 work. Nothing live was dropped: every live fix and every database migration is here

Invite people with just an ID: A-1101, A 1101 and A/1101 are the same person; an ID that is not on the list waits for your yes or no. The ID-only switch with name, location and ID (ID_ONLY) is still there and still off unless it is turned on
Payment is made in the console only: the game takes the console's signed paid notice once per order id, and the old pay and sign-in pages are behind switches that are off
The console speaks to you as 'you' and the Rupee sign is used on every screen and mail; one privacy line; the fairness sentence is proved by a test
Wrong employee IDs are counted per network (one IPv6 /64 counts as one) in one step, and the help text now says an ID is matched to a list and does not prove who types it
An older game that already holds IDs written the old way still matches them, so nobody on a list is locked out
The server itself now refuses an open game: 'anyone with the link' is refused and a game that says nothing is a game for the people on its list
The console can ask this game what must be paid for a game, and whether it can be paid, before it takes any money (payInfo); it gets the pack size, never a price
Coming in 1.6.0: 'You start the game' and 'You call the numbers' (the live site does not have them either)

title: The Corporate Games look: new website, one logo, six-item menu
changes: Every public page now looks and feels like the Corporate Tambola website: warm colours, the Corporate Bingo badge with CORPORATE above the name, the same header, footer, buttons and fonts
The header menu has six items: How it works, Free demo game, Guide, Brochure, Refer & earn, Log in
New pages: How it works and Guide (the organizer guide); the Brochure is a web page with the one-page PDF to download
One Corporate Games bar at the top of every public page; new app icons, share picture and e-mail header in the same brand
The organizer console and the phone pages wear the same colours, fonts and header bar. Nothing in how the console works has changed
Wording: close group everywhere, shorter plain sentences; the old organizer-guide address points to the Guide

title: A game waiting for payment never blocks a new game
changes: Only drafts that were never published count toward the limit of ten drafts; a game that is published but not yet paid for no longer stops an Organizer or Host from making a new game
Making a copy of a game follows the same rule

title: Bigger daily write guard
changes: The daily database-write guard is raised to 2,000,000 (a runaway guard only), because the account is on the paid Workers plan; a crowd joining together no longer meets a 'very busy' answer from the guard

title: Same hardening as Corporate Tambola 1.3.3: joining, permissions, messages, simpler console
changes: Joining: an employee ID or mobile number is checked against the organizer's list, a stranger waits for the organizer's yes, one phone cannot play as another (device proof on every card action), the same person joining twice gets the same card
A join that gets no answer (slow link, busy moment) is asked again by itself, safe because the same person always gets the same card
Permissions: a Co-host who has not accepted the terms cannot pay, a delete is refused while the game is being played, a Host's narrow link cannot change controls
Simpler console: the rarely used 'How many rounds' choice is hidden, never disabled; one game is one round
A demo link (zc.html?pass=) is used once, also when the console opens straight into a game
Players' data is deleted 20 hours after the end (the promise stays 24 hours) and a lazy tick runs the housekeeping when the scheduled job is late
Every refusal now says what happened, where, and how to fix it (guide catalog)
Big screen shows 'Connection lost' when the public clock does not answer for 15 seconds

title: One-door sign-in and e-mail-first console
changes: One sign-in door for Organizers and Hosts with a six-box code screen
A confirmed Host's e-mail is answered 'exists' (a code is sent)
Console keeps the state of each step

title: Colourful cards, Help Desk, guided errors
changes: Colour and phone-fit work, installable app
Help Desk helper flow
Plain-words errors with a Take-me-there button

title: Corporate Bingo goes live
changes: 75-ball Bingo on its own Cloudflare stack
Cards for every guest, winners decided by the software from the public numbers
Payment through the central payment service, report by e-mail
